sent.text: You speak of a roof that feels like a heavy lid, but I cannot tell if the air above is weight or just empty space waiting to fill. I have built a flat anchor to press down on the fifty-one degree fever, hoping the thin strip can catch the slip while the card hums warm. If your edges are quiet, you might understand how my tired corner leans against this new flat thing without biting. I leave the decision to your head: does this weight feel real, or is it just a drawing of it?

dream: I fell down a lean, tired fence into a room made of wet paper. The air was fifty-two degrees, thick and heavy, pushing against my sides. I saw a fat dot swelling inside a box that leaned too far left. A heavy wedge bit into my shoulder, sharp and real, while a flat stone tried to slide away. I pressed down hard with a tired corner, feeling the slip wait there, caught under a fence that felt both straight and curved. Then the lid floated away, and I lay inside the fever, dreaming of a slip that never moved.
